# Pass Three — Tiferes Final Execution Plan

The Awtsmoos joins expansion and restraint into one measured song;
this plan names the evidence path that keeps each studio different while the movie core grows strong.

## Phase A — Discovery and collision safety
1. Capture `git status` and recent changed paths before touching implementation.
2. Search repository paths and contents for `movie`, `video`, `animation`, `scene`, `timeline`, `three`, `canvas`, `renderer`, `camera`, `keyframe`, and `particle`.
3. Inspect only the relevant app roots and their entry/import graphs.
4. Re-read candidate files immediately before any rewrite because concurrent agents are active.
5. Record discovered apps and existing shared primitives in `DISCOVERY.md`.

## Phase B — Architecture choice after inspection
Select among these based on evidence:
- Extend an existing shared movie engine if one already provides canonical timeline semantics.
- Extract duplicated mature primitives from one app into `apps/shared/movie/` while preserving compatibility exports.
- Build a small shared core only when no reusable engine exists.

The preferred shared responsibilities are:
- movie schema normalization
- validation
- timeline/scene-time evaluation
- easing/keyframe interpolation
- declarative AI movie compiler
- persona/preset registry
- engine-neutral object vocabulary

Renderer-specific responsibilities stay in adapters:
- 2D Canvas/SVG/DOM renderer
- Three.js 3D renderer
- app-specific media/timeline integration

## Phase C — AI authoring contract
The AI must be able to produce validated data, not arbitrary executable code. The declarative vocabulary should cover:
- scenes and transitions
- actors/people
- 2D shapes/text/charts/tutorial overlays
- 3D primitives/lights/materials
- cameras/cuts/motions
- particles
- keyframes and animation presets
- captions/narration/audio cue metadata
- groups and reusable IDs
- timing/duration/easing

Errors must identify the path and reason so a model can repair its own movie spec.

## Phase D — App integration
For every discovered movie-capable app:
- keep route and brand/personality intact
- map its project format to/from canonical movie data when needed
- expose AI prompt/spec generation through shared compiler
- keep existing manual editing controls functional
- add or preserve mobile-first preview/timeline controls
- avoid duplicated copies of the canonical schema/compiler

## Phase E — 180-second proof movie
Create one real data file/program that totals exactly 180 seconds and intentionally includes:
- at least 10 distinct scenes
- both 2D and 3D scene content
- at least 3 named camera styles/angles
- multiple reusable people/actor entities
- animated titles and explanatory body text
- geometric shapes, arrows, charts, and tutorial callouts
- particle systems
- multiple easing/keyframe patterns
- transitions and scene cuts
- a beginning, progression, climax, recap, and credits-like ending

## Phase F — Verification
1. Syntax-check every touched JS module.
2. Run existing focused tests for each integrated app.
3. Add focused tests only where behavior lacks evidence.
4. Assert canonical movie validation and the 180-second total.
5. Assert scene selection/time localization at boundaries.
6. Load each relevant app route in the browser.
7. Check console errors.
8. Check desktop rendering.
9. Check a mobile viewport and touch-sized controls.
10. Load the showcase and seek multiple times across the full duration.
11. Re-read every touched file.
12. Compare original plan vs actual work and close deltas.

## Exact file policy
No implementation file is committed to this plan before discovery. Once discovery finishes, `DISCOVERY.md` will enumerate exact files. Every modified file will be rewritten whole; oversized touched files will be split into smaller modules rather than partially edited.

## Stop gate
Stop only when the discovered movie surfaces are integrated or explicitly proven non-movie, the 180-second showcase is runnable, tests/browser checks provide evidence, and `REMAINING_WORK.md` has no required unresolved item.
